title.rendered: How much to spend on your bachelor’s degree in India?

content.rendered:
There is an increasing trend to go to foreign countries for studies, due to better facilities and employment opportunities. India is one of the top destinations for foreign study. Every day major technological advances are being made seemingly in India. This is not the only reason that students are attracted to the country. Another reason is that the Indian government is also actively seeking to encourage and recruit international students and thus provides prestigious scholarships as well. If you are planning to pursue your bachelor’s in India, you must know about various important factors that will affect your stay there including the cost. This blog provides detailed information on how much to spend on your bachelor’s degree. 

A bachelor’s degree is an academic degree earned for an undergraduate course of study that could range in length of time. In India, a bachelor’s degree course duration is usually three to four years depending on the course you choose. Some of the popular bachelor’s degrees in India are Bachelor in Technology, Bachelor of Science (BSc), Bachelor of Arts (BA) and Bachelor of Law (LL.B.), Bachelor of Business Administration (B.BA), amongst others. The cost of a college degree in India varies significantly. The annual fee also depends on the college and course you choose to pursue. Generally, government educational institutes are a lot cheaper than private ones, and medicine or engineering will have higher annual fees than other courses of study. However, if you compare the cost of an Indian institute with American and European educational institutes, it is one of the least costly study abroad destinations in the world. 

Though tuition fees vary across private and public institutes, the average cost of tuition fees in India would be approximate $3000 USD per annum. Some expensive educational institutions are Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), SRM University, BITS, Manipal, Thapar Institute of Technology, Symbiosis International University, Amity University, etc. In Manipal Institutes, the fees start from around $5000 USD per semester whereas the fees of the Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) start from $3000 USD per semester onwards. In the case of Symbiosis International University, the fees can cost up to $7000 USD per semester. However, they have a good rankings and recongnisations, better percentage of Placements, lot of facilities for the students to prevail. The fees of Amity University start from $4000 USD for the courses per annum.

Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology (KIIT) is one of the prestigious educational institutions of India. The fees of KIIT can cost around $6000 USD approx per annum depending on the subject you choose. However, they offer KIIT University International Scholarship Program (KUISP) for International Students. Under this scheme, students can get for $1750 USD per semester or 1.5 lakhs INR per semester to Nepalese Students depending on courses. The University provides various facilities to its students such as AC hostels, free laptop, gyms, sports complexes, and hospitals etc. Similarly, there are an adequate number of classrooms in each campus for 30,000 students enrolled in KIIT University. KIIT has also good rankings and recognisations like VIT, SRM, Manipal, Amity, Symbiosis and better placemnets percentage than these universities. Classrooms are air conditioned and designed as per the international standard. The courses in this University include Engineering, Nursing, Biotechnology, Management, Law, and Medicine. 

However, every student cannot afford expensive universities. These students may have to support their family financially or they may even do a part time job to pay the bills. This does not mean that there aren’t any cheaper universities. As has been already mentioned above, the tuition fees vary according to the universities as well as the course you choose. If you are looking for a university with a lesser fee but equally good quality of education, R.K University can be the perfect university for you. The course fee is about $2000 USD per semester for Non-SAARC INR 2 lakhs per semester for SAARC Students. However, they are offering Presidential Scholarship, under this scheme the fee is about $1500 USD per annum for Non- SAARC and 1 lakh INR per annum for SAARC depending upon the courses. The courses available in RKU are in the field of Physiotherapy, Pharmacy, Ayurveda, Sciences, Engineering, Agriculture, and Management. The university also offers high-speed Wi-Fi, state of art laboratories, classrooms, libraries, seminar halls, sports building, and gymnasium. 

Before you rush to enroll in any university, make sure to compare the prices, course structure and accessibility of those universities. This will help you find a suitable university for your financial stability and you won’t have to worry in the future.

title.rendered: Pros and Cons of Online Classes

content.rendered:
Due to the coronavirus pandemic, most colleges and universities have paused their physical class and started online classes instead. However, online learning has its own set of positives and negatives. Here is a list of some of the pros and cons of online classes.

Pros of Online Class

1. Online Class is Flexible

It allows you to study anywhere you want. You can study in your pajamas. You can spend time with your family and friends. Even when you are sick, instead of being absent, you can listen to your teachers and gain some knowledge. Therefore, the online class offers flexibility.

2.  Online Class is Convenient

In an online class, everything is available to you. You can get announcements, access notes, review assignments, take practice quizzes, discuss questions, and chat with friends and study any time you want. Also, online lectures can be recorded, archived, and shared for future reference. This will help you access the learning material at a time of your comfort.

3. Online classes have Financial Benefits

It eliminates the cost points of student transportation, meals as well as hostel fees. You can study from the comfort of your home saving all this money. Also, as the course or study materials are available online, you don’t have to buy copies and notebooks. This creates a paperless learning environment that is more affordable and environment-friendly.

4. Online Class Improves Student Attendance 

As online classes are taken from the location of your choice, there is very little chance for you to miss your attendance. Even if you are ill, you can take your class by resting in your bed and listening to your professors.

 Cons of Online Class

1. Online classes may create a sense of isolation

During the virtual class, your only friend is your computer. You don’t have your friends beside you to talk to. This creates a sense of isolation for you. You will miss your friends who would gossip and make the class fun. You can request your teacher for online messages, emails and video conferencing that will allow for face-to-face interaction to reduce loneliness.

2. Online Class makes it easier to procrastinate

You tend to procrastinate a lot when you have virtual classes. As your teacher will not be there to reach you, you will find it easy to put off your readings as well as assignments. Therefore, make a schedule to complete your work on time.

3. Online classes require good time management skills

Due to online classes, you will have to spend your time on your computer screen. This will increase your screen time. You will find yourself buried beneath a seemingly insurmountable mountain of coursework. Also, you may tend to spend your whole day working. This will develop bad posture and other physical problems due to staying hunched in front of a screen.

4. Online Class gives you more freedom  

The virtual class gives you a lot of freedom. You can eat your food while studying. You can study in your bed with blankets on. This might turn out bad habit as when you are too comfortable, you may not focus on your studies. This freedom can be dangerous if you don’t learn how to handle it.

These were some pros and cons of online classes. Here are other blogs like this. Don’t forget to share on your social

.

If you are planning to study in India, Admizz is the best guide for you. For more information, follow us on Facebook , Instagram, Twitter  Linkedin .

title.rendered: How to Effectively Study in Groups?

content.rendered:
If you want a very effective strategy for studying, group study can be one of them. Study groups are particularly productive for completing projects, developing presentations, and preparing for exams. As groups share unique insights, they can learn from each other. Here are some tips that may help you conduct a more productive study group session. Effectively Studying in Groups can help you.

Form an Effective Study Group

Make sure to choose friends wisely. Choose those friends who are all committed to achieving a good grade. You can have at least 3 to 5 members in your study group. Meet up for two to three hours so that you can study well. Don’t let the study session be too long as productivity tends to drop and members of the group may lose focus. Depending on the subject matter, sometimes it’s advantageous to select group members with unique talents or knowledge.

  Show up prepared

Each member should come to the group prepared. Read all the chapters you are going to discuss with your friends. Remind them to study too. You should know what areas you are having difficulty with before attending the group study. This will help you to raise questions and get answers from your friends. Each member should review lecture notes, complete select readings from the textbook, and identify specific subjects to study.

  Stay organized and focused

When you are in a group study, the challenging part is you tend to lose focus quickly. Instead of studying, you might play video games or watch movies together. This will lead nowhere and your precious time is wasted. Therefore, make a group leader so that when you lose focus, they keep you back in track.

  Ensure participation

Every member of a study group should actively participate. A great way for each member to contribute is to assign specific topics and have each member instruct the group. Teaching is a great way for individuals to retain information.

  Pick an appropriate meeting place

It is really important to pick an appropriate meeting place so that the group doesn’t lose focus. Pick a place where no one can disturb you. It may be your or your friend’s house or your college library. It is best to study in environments without distractions and areas where group members can communicate freely.

  Set a study agenda

Make sure to let each member suggest topics to review, practice, or clarify. Bring questions to the group and discuss them. Listen to your friend’s answer as well as try to answer some. You can also take turns teaching or presenting homework problems.

  Take a Break

Studying for a longer period of time can make you dull. Therefore, take breaks in between. You can watch some videos or play a game during the breaks. This will help you to be focused. Effectively Studying in Groups can be best sometimes.

title.rendered: 12 Must Try Street Food of India

content.rendered:
With rich and diversified culture and tradition, India has a variety of foods as well. Indian street foods are known worldwide for their taste and diversity. Make sure to try these top 12 street foods of India when you visit.

Pav Bhaji

Pav Bhaji is a mixture of veggies with a few drops of lime to go with the pav dipped in butter. You should try this food, especially in winter. It is loved by locals and tourists at the same time.

Poha Jalebi

The poha is topped with sev, peanuts, and sometimes tomato and pomegranate, too. It is then served with piping hot jalebis. It is a light yet fulfilling breakfast option and is quite cheap as well.

   Chhole Bhature

Chhole Bhature is one of the most loved street food in India. The combination of puffy hot bhaturas with spicy and creamy chhole tastes like heaven. They taste best when served hot, they are yummy and filling.

 Gol Gappa

This street food has many names such as Pani Puri and Paani Ke Patashe. It is basically crispy atta or sooji puris, filled with tangy water, chickpeas, mashed potato, and a melange of spices. Every state in India has its own signature specialty.

   Dahi Puri

Dahi puri is similar to Gol Gappas but instead of tangy water, it is served with yogurt. This is a delicious street-side delicacy, which is loved by both kids and adults.

   Daulat Ki Chaat

This street food makes its appearance during the winter season only. Its creamy and frothy texture is derived from whisking sweetened milk for hours. It is then kept overnight in the open to soak in the dew. The garnishing of malai, khoya, pistachio, and powdered sugar gives this delight a mildly sweet taste. 

   Kathi Rolls

Kathi rolls are made with a delectable filling of kebabs and raw veggies. The filling is stuffed inside a maida-based paratha, which is flaky and crispy. Make sure to have one when you are in Calcutta.

   Dabeli

It is a spicy snack prepared as a mixture of special dabeli masala and boiled potatoes which is then put into a burger like a bun. The dish is accompanied by different chutneys like garlic, tamarind, date, chili, etc.

   Kanji Vada

Kanji Vadas are a local delicacy coming from Rajasthan and Gujarat. Kanji is flavored water that is fermented for a day to develop sourness. It has various spices like mustard powder, asafoetida, black salt, red chili powder, turmeric, etc.

Aloo Tikki

The mashed potatoes mixed up with spices are fried to get hot and crispy Tikkis. Sometimes served with Tamarind chutney and sometimes with a combo of tamarind and mint, this dish is a bomb of flavors. You can find this in every corner of the country.

Momos

No matter how much you eat these, they’ll never be enough. Though it is a Tibetan Dish, the North Indians here love it to the core. Adding the twists of masalas and stuffing, a massive variety of momos are sold.

Nagori Halwa And Bedmi Puri

These dal-stuffed puris are served with a spicy potato-based curry and sooji halwa. It is a complete meal in itself and is best relished when paired with a chilled glass of sweet lassi. It has a combination of sweet and savory flavors. 

These were famous street food of India. Make sure you taste this food when you visit India. To read more blogs like this. Click Here.  Don’t forget to share on your social.

If you are planning to study in India, Admizz is the best guide for you. 

For more information, follow us on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter,  Linkedin.

title.rendered: 6 Ways to Reduce Stress In College

content.rendered:
College life is not always about having fun with friends. There will be lots of stress about completing your assignments and projects, and examinations as well as making time for yourself. However, having stress is normal and you should not worry about having one much. There are lots of ways to help you reduce stress. Here we have collected the 6 best ways to reduce stress.

Get Enough Sleep

It is often said by our parents to study all the time instead of sleeping. But it is wrong. Sleep is really important for you to stay healthy. When it comes to stress, sleep is even more important. Therefore, take enough rest to decrease your stress level. Insufficient sleep can even put you at risk for serious illnesses, such as diabetes, obesity, and depression. An adult needs seven to nine hours of sleep. Thus, align your sleep schedule and get enough rest.

Eat Well

You may not feel it but a healthy diet really helps you to decrease your stress. Make sure to eat a diet that is rich in vegetables, fruits, and whole grains. When you are stressed, you will feel like eating junk foods. Afterward, you will feel tired and you look for the same junk food to kick you back up. This will be an endless cycle making you feel worse. Therefore, start eating healthy and avoid junk foods.

Exercise

When you exercise, your body releases endorphins. It is a feel-good chemical that acts as a natural painkiller and even improves sleep. Therefore, get up and do some exercise. Give yourself 20 minutes a day of physical activity and it will help to reduce your stress level. You can go swimming or do some yoga. If they are not your cup of tea, try walking or jogging.

Make a Plan

One of the reasons you can get stressed is when you don’t have a proper schedule and there is too much work to do. Instead of worrying in these times, just get organized and make a plan. You can buy a diary, write down your to-do list, prioritize your work and stick to it. This will not only lessen your burden but helps you give enough time to your friends and families as well.

To read more blogs like this. Click Here.  Don’t forget to share on your social.

If you are planning to study in India, Admizz is the best guide for you. For more information, follow us on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and Linkedin.

title.rendered: Student Visa and Permits in India

content.rendered:
Student Visas are granted to people who wish to come to India and study at an officially recognized educational institution. The main document required is student admission/registration papers from the institution.

 Duration and Validity

A Student Visa is valid for the period of study as approved by the educational institution in India. Usually, they are issued for up to five years, depending on the duration of the course. Student visas can be extended as well.

The Visa duration starts on the day of issuance, and not on the day of entry in India.

If you are planning to apply, you should apply for Student Visa at least 8 weeks in advance of your intended date of travel. However, people of Pakistani heritage should apply at least three months in advance. 

Fee for Student Visa

Visa fees for Student visas are different for all countries. It ranges from $13 to $118.

 Eligibility

Indian Missions/Posts grant a Student Visa for a period of five years or for the duration of the course of study, whichever is less, to the below:

  •     To foreigner students coming to India to pursue regular and full-time academic studies in India.
  •     For foreigner students coming for Industrial training, summer projects, and internships.
  •     Provisional student visa valid for six months for the students exploring admission or taking admission tests.
  •     Applicants should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course in a reputed/recognized educational institution in India and evidence of financial support.
  •     The applicant should also possess a “No Objection Certificate” from the Ministry of Health in case of admission to medical or Paramedical courses.
  •     Spouse and dependent family members accompanying the applicant must apply for an Entry Visa (Not Tourist Visa. Its termination date will coincide with the period of the principal visa holder.

 Provisional Visa

Sometimes you may not have a firm letter from the university or recognized educational institution due to reasons like pending admissions tests or other requirements. In such a case, a provisional visa can be issued on the basis of a provisional admission certificate/letter of offer issued by an institution in India.

A provisional visa is valid for 3 months. If admission is not given or confirmed within the stipulated period, the student will have to leave India. Extension of the provisional student visa is not allowed.

 Form

The interested students are required to fill out an online visa Application by visiting a website which website is http://indianvisaonline.gov.in/visa/ and visit their nearest embassy with a printout of the online filled application and required travel documents.

content.rendered:
It will be hectic for students to maintain time for their studies and personal life. There will be loads of assignments and projects to complete on time while you want to watch that show your friend has recommended to you. Not only this, but you also need some time for yourself to follow your passion. Therefore, time management skill is a must for students. Here is the list of seven best time management tips for you.

Make a Proper Schedule

When it comes to time management, the first thing you need to do is identify what your work is and prioritize the tasks you need to complete. Therefore, make a proper schedule for each day. You can buy a journal to keep track of your work. You can even use colorful markers to track your routine. Making a schedule and working accordingly will not only help you in your college life but in your professional as well.

Set Goals

After you made the list of things to do, set goals for the completion of your work. You can set goals for each study session. For example, you can set a goal to read six pages of text from your history book. Also, set a goal to not engage in any behavior during dedicated study time. This will help you to complete your assignment on time.

Eliminate distractions

It is easy to get distracted when you are working. Make sure to pay attention to what draws your focus away from your studies and assignments. It can be your cell phone or a neighbor playing loud music next door. Thus, when it’s time for studying, you can turn off your cell phone or ask your neighbor to slow down the music. It’s easy to become distracted by the news or your favorite celebrity gossip site. Thus, avoid surfing the web excessively.

Don’t multitask

Instead of watching a movie and doing your assignment simultaneously, focus on one thing at a time. You can complete your assignment first. Then, you can watch the movie. This way, you can remember what you studied as well and enjoy the movie without any disturbance. Always arrange your tasks in order of importance. Then pay attention to the crucial task that requires the most effort.

To read more blogs like this. Go to Admizz.com. Don’t forget to share on your social.

If you are planning to study in India, Admizz is the best guide for you.

title.rendered: How to Prepare Well for Exams

content.rendered:
We have been taking exams all our life. Examinations have been part of human life. However, whenever we have class tests or board exams, we tend to panic. We start to worry about how our exams will go a month before the exam. Also, the pressure of getting good grades makes us even more stressed. We tend to lose our sleep and feel anxious. If you also feel the same way when it comes to the examinations, you don’t have to worry anymore. There are several things that you can do to prepare more effectively for your exams. This article has listed some tips about how to Prepare Well for Exams.

Start Your Preparation Early

Many students have the habit of studying at the last minute. This will add more pressure as they cannot cover all the chapters in time. Therefore, start early with your exam preparation. You will have ample time to review everything you have already studied. You can also make a timetable to manage your time effectively. If you find some subjects harder than others, make sure to give them more study time.

Organize your Study Space

An unorganized space distracts you from studying effectively. Therefore, before you start studying, manage your study space. Clean the desks and arrange your notebooks properly. Make sure that your chair is comfortable and that there is enough lighting in your room. You can also sort out all your study material before beginning with the preparation. This will help you to stay focused during preparation offering you a comfortable environment.

Take Regular Breaks

You may feel like studying continuously for hours will make you productive. But this is not true at all. Studying for hours will only drain you out and make you tired. Therefore, take regular breaks between hours. For example, take a 5-minute break if you study for half an hour. This will help you in longer retention of information and freshen up your mind. You can listen to music or walk around the house during the break.

Do not Stay up all Night

Students tend to wake up all night and study one day before exams. This is completely wrong. This will only make you more anxious and stressed out. Instead, you should review what you have already studied and sleep early. You will also feel refreshed on the day of your exam if you follow this rule.

Plan your Exam Day and Sleep Well

Make sure everything is ready in advance before the exam day. Check if you have all your necessary belongings and admit cards with you. Do not leave anything for the last day. Also, do not forget to take at least a minimum of seven hours of sleep before the exam. If you are sleep-deprived, you might not be able to complete your exam in time or justify your answers correctly.

Do Not Evaluate Post ExaminationAfter finishing their exams, most students will calculate how many marks they will score. This is a very bad habit as this will give anxiety to the students. Therefore instead of calculating the marks, stay focused on your studies and prepare for the next exam to ensure that you do not repeat the same mistake again.

These were some of the tips about how to prepare well for exams.

Here are 10 interesting facts about India. It is a beautiful country with a diversity of culture and geography which you will love about India.

Home of a mysterious skeleton lake

Located in the Himalayas at about 16,470 feet, the glacial Lake Roopkund has become famous for the human skeletons found in the lake and surrounding areas. It is believed that the skeletons are the remains of people from the 9th century who perished during a severe hail storm.

A village with no locks and doors may be the safest on Earth

The village of Shani Shingnapur is famous for not having a door or lock on a single house. Beyond that, there has not been a recording of a criminal act for almost 400 years. Its residents sleep soundly as they believe Lord Shani to be the guardian of the town. Many people think that the shared vulnerability has created a neighborly trust between the residents, which has formed protection stronger than a deadbolt or heavy gate.

North Sentinel Island is one of the last “untouched” places on Earth

The Indian government has prohibited anyone from going within three miles of North Sentinel Island, home of the Sentinelese people. In 1991, the anthropologist Madhumala Chattophadhyay had several peaceful encounters with the Sentinelese. But in subsequent years, the people made it very clear (sometimes violently) that they did not want to be disturbed. It is now considered one of the last places untouched by the outside world.

The Kumbh Mela is visible from space

The Kumbh Mela is an important festival and pilgrimage site, and the largest gathering on Earth. While a celebration takes place each year, there is a festival of greater significance at four-year and twelve-year intervals. The number of people attending the festival is so large that the crowd is visible in satellite photos taken from space.

Snakes and Ladders originated in India

Earlier known as Moksha Patamu, the game was initially invented as a moral lesson about karma to be taught to children. It was later commercialized and has become one of the most popular board games in the world.

Mysterious Anti-Gravity Hills In Ladakh, Magnetic Hill

With the anti-gravitational effect, this is the only magnetic hill in India. Landmarked by a yellow notice board that spells out instructions and asks you to place your car on neutral gear right on the spot marked by white paint, this one will leave you in awe as your car will begin to move uphill on its own.

Indian National Kabaddi Team Has Won all World Cups

India is where the game of Kabaddi originated, and the Indian national Kabaddi team makes sure it brings all the 5 World Cup trophies home. The women’s Kabaddi team has also remained undefeated in all the Kabaddi World Cups.

The steel wires in the Bandra Worli Sealink could stretch around the world

Completed in 2010, the incredible Bandra Worli Sealink Bridge required 90,000 tons of cement to build. To hold that all up, enormous steel cables – each with the ability to hold up 900 tons of weight – were put in place along the bridge. If they were laid out end to end, the cables could reach around the circumference of the globe.

World’s Only Floating Post Office in Dal Lake in Srinagar

India does not only have the largest network of postal services in the world, but it has some very unique post offices, including one that floats on the water. The floating post office is located on Dal Lake in Srinagar. Perched on a houseboat, it also includes a philately museum within itself.

Around 70% of the world’s spices come from India

India is by far the largest producer of spices, which are shipped across continents to restaurants and kitchens worldwide. Some of the best-known spices are turmeric, cumin, saffron, and chili powders.

These are some interesting facts about India. Hope this information is informative for you.

title.rendered: Mobile Apps For a Smooth Stay In India

content.rendered:
If we look back at human development and evolution, we have come a long way from traditional and simple lifestyles to modern and scientific livelihoods. Thousands of years ago, our ancestors used to hunt for food. Whereas now with a single click on your mobile phone, the food is delivered to you. The development of various technologies has made our life a lot easier. With a mobile phone in your hand, you can now conquer the whole world. Nowadays, you don’t even need a friend as various mobile applications provide you company and assistance 24/7. If you are planning to study in India or if you are already residing in India, here is the list of must-have apps that help you to live a hustle-free life in India.

 Google Translate

English is the common language in various parts of India. However, if you don’t know Hindi or understand other state languages, you might get in trouble. Just install Google Translate on your phone and communicate freely. When you are traveling in a remote part of the country, this app is really helpful. It provides a smooth translation in regional Indian languages to bridge any lingual gaps.

 Google Maps Navigation

Google Maps Navigation is one of the most used mobile applications not only in India but throughout the world. Wondering where the next train station is or forgot your college route? If you have this app on your phone, you don’t have to worry even for a second. You can download this app on both Android and iOS smartphones. You can also alternate directions, and estimates of traffic that you might delay your journey.

 PhonePe/Google Pay

You carry cash nowadays, right? Google Pay can be used to make bill payments, book events, and send money to users in your contact list. It also accepts payments in the form of almost 100 currencies from around the world. Similar to this, there are other apps such as PayTM, Freecharge, and RazorPay that are widely used in India.

BookMyShow/Paytm Insider

Student life is not about studying for 24 hours and getting good grades in exams. It’s about having fun, making memories, and living life to the fullest. India is a multicultural country with festivals happening every now and then. It might be difficult for you to track all the gigs happening in the country. Therefore, the apps such as BookMyShow and Paytm Insider will not only provide a detailed selection of events but let you book your seats instantly as well.

 Zomato/Swiggy

Sometimes you get tired of eating your hostel food. You miss the home-cooked meals that your mother used to make for you. In those days, you can simply order from your favorite restaurants with the help of apps like Zomato and Swiggy. They provide you with lists based on cuisine and budget preferences. After you’ve made your pick, they’ll deliver it to you. With UberEats, you can even track your food.

 Spotify/ Amazon Prime Music

Who doesn’t listen to music, right? Music is your best friend when you are traveling alone on the bus or train. It helps you to relax and gives words to your emotions. Spotify and Amazon Prime Music provide you with millions of songs of your choice. They have a playlist and libraries based on the individual’s musical taste and preferences.

 These applications cost no money to download. They can be your perfect partner in the time of your needs. So, download them now to make your stay in India a smooth and rewarding experience.

title.rendered: Which is better KIIT vs MNNIT ?

content.rendered:
Comparing KIIT and MNNIT, both the institution are of the same value. Taking some facts and resources here we have.

KIIT was established in 1992 whereas MNNIT was established in 1961. KIIT is privately deemed to be a university whereas MNNIT is a fully funded government Institution.

In this short duration, KIIT is climbing the ladder of rankings and recognition. It holds the most prestigious title of Institution of Eminence which is given to only 10 government and 10 private Institutions in the country by the MHRD Government of India. Taking some facts from NIRF rankings, in 2018, 2019 and 2020 KIIT ranked 51, 48, and 42 respectively. Whereas MNNIT ranked 48, 42, and 48 in consecutive years 2018, 2019, and 2020.

Comparing facts of NIRF 2020

On Teaching Learning and Resources KIIT scored 66.08% and MNNIT scored 59.71%. Research and Professional Practice KIIT scored 25.8% and MNNIT scored 30.56%. Under Graduations Outcome KIIT scored 65.80% and MNNIT scored 69%. Outreach and Inclusivity KIIT scored 75.70 and MNNIT scored 50.72%. The perception of KIIT is scored 17.79% and MNNIT scored 22.89%. Overall KIIT scored 50.07% whereas MNNIT scored 48.24% in NIRF rankings 2020.

Another factor to compare is Placement at their campus.

MNNIT has an average of 85% placements for UG and PG students with an average package of 7.95L and the highest as 30L. KIIT has an average of 88% placements for UG and 100% placements for PG with an average of 3.5L and the highest of 30L.

In the end, we say, it’s a student’s choice to go to a government college or private. Yes, getting into MNNIT will be a tough task whereas at KIIT one can get into it with the fulfillment of the minimum criteria for International students.

title.rendered: 7 inspirational Movies that students must watch

content.rendered:
Movies are an excellent way to learn. In fact, watching movies helps students grasp concepts and expand their vocabulary. Even if you need to learn a new language, watching movies in that language can help them realize the effect of the words and phrases used. Students need motivation and inspiration in order to achieve their goals. 

As you face your studies, you may find yourself in a situation where the work isn’t easy but there is something else that will definitely inspire you to give it your best shot. Like when you’re working hard at something and get stuck, or experience some setbacks. When these things happen in life, you end up being self-critical rather than looking beyond your current circumstance. But taking a step back and seeing how things should be can be very helpful. 

There are plenty of movies out there that can inspire students, but not all of them are created equal. Here’s a list of seven inspirational movies that students must watch. These movies can help you get out of your self-doubt and feel better about yourself. To help you empathize with the characters, they are set up so you can relate to them. All of these films are also inspirational, which makes them even more effective. Let’s take a look at some of the best motivational movies that college students should watch!

Dead Poets Society

‘Dead Poets Society’ is a 1959 American teen drama film starring the famous actor and comedian Robin Williams. Set at a Vermont boarding school named Welton Academy, it’s about a group of kids attending a boarding school in 1959. In his academic career, Robin Williams played the character of John Keating who changed the way students viewed poetry and literature. He encouraged students to embrace their individuality and live their lives to the fullest. It inspires you to “seize the day” and make a difference.

As you watch The Dead Poet’s Society, you will start questioning everything. You will start looking for joy in life in more subtle ways, and you will cry for days after the movie ends. It’s a must-see film for everyone.

Whiplash

In Whiplash, Miles Teller plays Andrew Niemann (played by Miles Teller), a nineteen-year-old who dreams of becoming the greatest jazz drummer in the world. The movie is a powerful statement that greatness doesn’t come easily; it takes your best effort and sacrifice to achieve it. You will feel empowered to do more, push your limits, and never settle for anything less than you deserve after watching this movie.

The Shawshank Redemption

Directed by Frank Darabont, this is a story about Andy Dufresne, an inmate who is sentenced to life in prison for the murder of his wife and her lover. 

This movie is one of the best inspirational movies that teach us how to never give up, even when things don’t seem good. Andy Dufresne was sent to prison for killing his wife and her lover. But prison life turns out to be a lot more than he expected, as he realizes that there are some good people among the inmates. After he is released from prison, he becomes friends with Tim Robbins’ character Red. The two form a bond that lasts even after Andy is released from prison again. This movie will make you cry because it makes you realize how good life can be if you just give up on yourself and stop being so self-critical.

The Social Network 

 The Social Network is a 2010 American drama film, directed by David Fincher and written by Aaron Sorkin. The film stars Jesse Eisenberg as Mark Zuckerberg, Rooney Mara as Erica Albright, Justin Timberlake as Sean Parker, Andrew Garfield as Eduardo Saverin and Armie Hammer as Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss.

The Social Network is based on the book by Ben Mezrich. The film has been nominated for Best Picture at the Academy Awards as well as Best Screenplay (for Aaron Sorkin), Best Performance by an Actor (Jesse Eisenberg), and Best Supporting Actor (Justin Timberlake).

This movie is about the founding of Facebook and how it all started. It follows the story of its founder, Mark Zuckerberg, and his best friend, Eduardo Saverin. The movie is based on real life events and has a lot of drama in it. It also shows how Mark Zuckerberg became a billionaire by selling his company to Yahoo for $1 billion in cash and stock.

The Theory of Everything

The Theory of Everything is a 2014 British biographical drama film based on the life of physicist Stephen Hawking. The film stars Eddie Redmayne as Stephen Hawking and Felicity Jones as his wife, Jane Wilde. Redmayne was cast after a worldwide search for an actor to portray Hawking, and filming took place in the United Kingdom, California, New York City and London.

Directed by James Marsh, The Theory of Everything deals with Hawking’s early life, when he fell in love with his first wife (Jones) who died young after being diagnosed with motor neuron disease. They had two children together: Robert (Redmayne), who has autism; and Timothy (Jonas Armstrong), who has Down syndrome.

The Theory of Everything is the biography of one of the greatest scientists in history – one of the greatest scientists in history. As actor Eddie Redmayne portrays the scientist outstandingly, you will be taken on a roller coaster ride of emotion and euphoria. Despite Hawking’s tragic medical condition, The Theory of Everything is a wonderful tribute to his achievements. The movie inspires you to remain hopeful and persevere despite everything.

The Man Who Knew Infinity

The Man Who Knew Infinity is a book by the Indian writer and physicist Srinivasa Ramanujan. The story is about Srinivasa Ramanujan, a mathematics prodigy who lived in India and corresponded with the Cambridge University mathematician G. H. Hardy. In his twenties, Ramanujan had already made significant contributions to several fields of mathematics, including number theory, infinite series, and continued fractions.

The title refers to Riemann’s famous conjecture; Ramanujan proved this conjecture for prime numbers less than 2n + 1. Although it was not published in his lifetime (he died at age 32), it was discovered by his nephew nearly 40 years after his death. The text contains many other results as well.

It tells the story of humanity’s genius and inspires readers to dream and fight for what they love despite hardships. The Man Who Knew Infinity makes you realize talent alone is not enough to achieve success. Yes, you have the brains, you have worked hard, but you must also utilize your resources and seize every opportunity when it arises.

Warrior 

Warrior is a 2011 American biographical drama film directed by Gavin O’Connor and starring Tom Hardy, Nick Nolte, Joel Edgerton, and Sam Rockwell. The film is inspired by the life of the late Patrick Swayze. It was released on June 8, 2011, in the United States.

The film centers on Swayze’s life from his childhood to his rise to fame as a dancer and actor in Hollywood films during the 1980s with co-stars including Demi Moore, Charlie Sheen, Jennifer Beals, and Donnie Wahlberg.

This is the story of a real man, who was a warrior, who fought battles. He was always ready to fight for what he believed in and he never backed down from a fight. He was the kind of guy that you wanted on your side in any kind of battle.

There are a number of fantastic shots showing MMA fighting with the major theme being forgiveness and the redemption of the human spirit. The strength of family bonds is also explored well in the film.

Conclusion:

These seven movies serve as excellent examples of how to motivate oneself in life. Since student life is an emotionally and mentally challenging time, it is especially important for students to understand how to muster up the willpower needed to get through their courses. All of these movies showcase various obstacles to success but take a novel approach to solve them by using emotion. Regardless of what career path you choose, the message these movies send is universal—when you persevere and hold on to your passion, you will reach your goals.

Motivational movies are like the best pick-me-ups on a bad day, and they have the power to change the way you feel about everything. The lesson that we learned from this list is that there’s a motivational movie for just about everybody. There are movies for students, bibliophiles, athletes, writers, and others. So if you’re looking for some motivation to get you through your day or study session, then one of these films is sure to help.

title.rendered: 10 Inspirational Books Every College Student must Read

content.rendered:
Reading is a complicated developmental task that has been linked to many other developmental achievements, including attention, memory, language, and motivation. Or simply to say reading is learning. The basic ingredient to learn was, is, and always will be Reading.

The one habit that every college student must build themselves is to read. A college student is always tangled among college assignments, social life, and their precious hobbies but if you do not have time to read then you will definitely lack development. That is why the following books are the greatest inspirational books that every college student must read in order to build and figure out their life.

The Magic Of Thinking Big

An American motivational author and coach David Joseph Schwartz, Jr. is the author of The Magic of Thinking Big. This book was written in 1959. 

The keys to maximizing your career, marital, and family life may be found in The Magic of Thinking Big. The book serves as an example of how you may achieve the success you desire without being exceptionally bright or original. All you need to do is think in a way that fosters success. By setting lofty goals for yourself, you may inspire yourself to work more, make more money, and live a happier, more fulfilling life.

The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari

The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari is written by Robin Sharma in 1996 known to be a great motivational author for his many works. 

The book’s main lesson is how to create a life that ensures contentment and happiness over the long term. It enlightens you that giving more attention to developing your inner life than your outside existence is crucial. One should not always run after financial or material success.

Think and Grow Rich

Think and Grow Rich is a book published in 1937 by Napolean Hill.

The concept of the book is based on the notion that mental imagery and imagination may be used to achieve success in any effort. Simply said, you can become anything that your mind allows you to become. As a consequence, your mind is the only thing that has the power to either prohibit you from becoming the finest version of yourself or to encourage you to do so.

Rich Dad, Poor Dad

Rich Dad Poor Dad was published in 1997 by Robert T. Kiyosaki and Sharon Lechter.

The Power of Now is to profound practice as Rich Dad, Poor Dad is to financial knowledge. It gives you a complete set of solid, essential guidelines for living better and more successfully in relation to money and personal finances. The book makes use of the contrast between the two characters, “poor father” and “rich father,” to illustrate various financial standards. Rich Dad, Poor Dad is the appropriate collection of insightful advice and enlightening knowledge if you need to increase your ability to manage your finances.

The Power of Positive Thinking

Norman Vincent Peale wrote The Power of Positive Thinking in 1952.

We are compelled to see and appreciate our power by the Power of Positive Thinking. It teaches us that if anything is fragile in the world, it is not us but rather our difficulties and challenges. We may learn to face our anxieties and conquer obstacles. Success won’t start knocking on our door until then.

How to Win Friends and Influence People

How to Win Friends and Influence People was published in 1936 by Dale Carnegie.

The self-help classic reads like a guide to living. The fundamental element is that modifying your own conduct is all it takes to influence others’ actions. It imparts the knowledge necessary to better understand people, make friends more easily, build stronger bonds with coworkers, and persuade others to follow your direction.

The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People

The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People was published by Stephen R. Covey in 1989.

You may transition from a dependent condition to independence and then interdependence using the seven habits in this book. While society and the majority of self-help books on the market promote independence as the pinnacle of success, Covey contends that interconnectedness produces the best outcomes.

The Power of Habit

Charles Duhigg wrote The Power of Habit in 2012.

The Power of Habit makes a compelling case that knowing how habits function is essential to attaining success in a variety of areas, including regular exercise, weight loss, raising outstanding kids, increasing productivity, and creating ground-breaking businesses and social movements.

Thinking, Fast and Slow

Daniel Kahneman, a psychologist, published the book Thinking, Fast and Slow in 2011.

The book explains how two competing systems in your brain are always vying for control of your behavior and actions, and it shows you how this may cause mistakes in memory, judgment, and decision-making as well as what you can do to fix them.

 Emotional Intelligence

Emotional Intelligence is a book written in 1995 by Daniel Goleman.

The book tells us that emotional intelligence is just as crucial to success as IQ in all spheres of one’s life, including academic, professional, social, and interpersonal ones. It is defined as “a type of social intelligence that entails the capacity to monitor one’s own sentiments and emotions and those of others, to distinguish between them, and to utilize this knowledge to inform one’s thinking and action.”

Conclusion

Reading a good book is a definitive investment upon you, yourself. It offers knowledge, ideas, and inspiration to make your daily life richer. Reading these inspirational and motivational books may help you develop a good outlook on life and help you stay inspired and motivated. While there are specific things in your life that you have to face yourself, some of the things are common and can be easily learned as these books are written by the people who have devoted their lives to sharing these experiences. Always remember reading was, is, and always will be the basic ingredient of learning.

title.rendered: Why To Study in India After 12th?

content.rendered:
“What comes next?” Among the generation of students in the 12th standard, this question is frequently asked. The questions affect thousands of students annually, both in India and overseas. Regarding potential career paths, employment chances, and yes, even their passion and inclination, there is a misunderstanding among them. Counselors claim that the absence of accurate information on the courses offered in India and their employment prospects is partially to blame. 

Students can choose between science, commerce, and the arts as appropriate post-secondary alternatives. The decision to enroll in a course should always be extremely inspiring for the students rather than a convenient option. When selecting a degree to follow after their 12th-grade education in India, students must take their interests, motivation, and ambitions into account. 

Engineering, Architecture, Design, Law, Applied Science, Business Studies, Management, Behavioral and Social Sciences, Economics, Media, Humanities, and more prominent fields are available for students to pick from.

Most Importantly why India?

The richness and history of India give every student a wealth of alternatives. Like the nation itself, India has a broad and diversified educational system. Even while living in India might be difficult for international students, it can be a pleasant and inexpensive experience.

A civilization that has existed for millennia, the birthplace of four major global religions, a stunning variety of cultures, languages, and customs, and unimaginable natural beauty, from the towering Himalayas to the Rajasthani deserts. Instead of asking “why to study in India?” the actual question is “why wouldn’t you?” India not only has a lot to offer tourists, but it also has a lot to give students. Studying in India has a lot to offer, whether your interests are in politics or computers, classics or diversity because it is a fast developing nation at the forefront of the technological revolution.

Learning in India is unlike studying anyplace else because of the vastness and diversity of its educational system, which mirrors the country’s history. With 3.5 million students, Indira Gandhi National Open University is the largest university in the world by enrolment. There are 575 university-level institutions in India’s higher education system, including:

  • The National Department of Higher Education has responsibility over 42 core universities.
  • State governments oversee 243 public universities.
  • 53 privately owned universities out of 130 designated institutions that operate independently.
  • 33 national institutions of importance, which are regarded as being of particular significance and usually concentrate on science and technology.

Furthermore, there are approximately 30,000 institutions operating in India that provide more specialized education, frequently in technical subjects like engineering. No matter what their interests are, international students in India may choose a program that suits them thanks to all these alternatives.

India’s degree system, which awards bachelor’s, master’s, and doctorate degrees, is influenced by British higher education.

More details about certain Indian institutions and the higher education system are available from the Department of Higher Education of the Indian Government.

Following secondary school, students can use the list of courses in the three streams described above to make an intelligent decision that fits with their interests and professional goals.

Art Students Course

Though there is a list of courses that would provide you strong employment prospects after completing your 12th grade in the arts, there are some students who believe that choosing the arts stream will give them fewer career opportunities than choosing science or commerce.

  • BBA- Bachelor of Business Administration
  • BMS- Bachelor of Management Science
  • BFA- Bachelor of Fine Arts
  • BEM- Bachelor of Event Management
  • Integrated Law Course- BA + LL.B
  • BJMC- Bachelor of Journalism and Mass Communication
  • BFD- Bachelor of Fashion Designing
  • BSW- Bachelor of Social Work
  • BBS- Bachelor of Business Studies
  • BTTM- Bachelor of Travel and Tourism Management

Aviation Courses

  • B.Sc- Interior Design
  • B.Sc.- Hospitality and Hotel Administration
  • Bachelor of Design (B. Design)
  • Bachelor of Performing Arts
  • BA in History

After-second-grade courses for Science Faculty

There are several alternatives for college studies after finishing your 12th-grade science coursework. Engineering courses are available to students who are interested in technical education, and the remaining students can select from the courses mentioned below:

  • BE/B.Tech- Bachelor of Technology
  • B.Arch- Bachelor of Architecture
  • BCA- Bachelor of Computer Applications
  • B.Sc.- Information Technology
  • B.Sc- Nursing
  • BPharma- Bachelor of Pharmacy
  • B.Sc- Interior Design
  • BDS- Bachelor of Dental Surgery
  • Animation, Graphics, and Multimedia
  • B.Sc. – Nutrition & Dietetics
  • BPT- Bachelor of Physiotherapy
  • B.Sc- Applied Geology
  • BA/B.Sc. Liberal Arts
  • B.Sc.- Physics
  • B.Sc. Chemistry
  • B.Sc. Mathematics

Following high school, you have a choice of many B. Tech programs, including One of the prominent fields that offer a large selection of technical courses, is science. For students who have finished their secondary education in the science stream, below is a list of engineering courses.

  • Automobile Engineering
  • Civil Engineering
  • Computer Science and Engineering
  • Biotechnology Engineering
  • Electrical and Electronics Engineering
  • Electronics and Communication Engineering
  • Automation and Robotics
  • Petroleum Engineering
  • Instrumentation Engineering
  • Ceramic Engineering
  • Chemical Engineering
  • Structural Engineering
  • Transportation Engineering
  • Construction Engineering
  • Power Engineering
  • Robotics Engineering
  • Textile Engineering
  • Smart Manufacturing & Automation

For Management/Commerce Stream

Students may choose the commerce stream after the tenth grade if they wish to study finance and management. Since mathematics is an elective for commerce majors, those who are interested in the subject but do not wish to pursue a career in science can enroll in commerce while taking math.

  • B.Com- Bachelor of Commerce
  • BBA- Bachelor of Business Administration
  • B.Com (Hons.)
  • BA (Hons.) in Economics
  • Integrated Law Program- B.Com LL.B.
  • Integrated Law Program- BBA LL.B

Students may choose the commerce stream after the tenth grade if they wish to study finance and management. Since mathematics is an elective for commerce majors, those who are interested in the subject but do not wish to pursue a career in science can enroll in commerce while taking math.

  • CA- Chartered Accountancy
  • CS- Company Secretary
  • Bachelor of Design in Accessory Design, Fashion Design, Ceramic Design, Leather Design, Graphic Design, Industrial Design, Jewelry Design
  • Bachelor in Foreign Language
  • Diploma Courses
  • Advanced Diploma Courses
  • Certificate Courses

Students can pick from a list of courses offered in India thanks to the information provided above.

Conclusion

Studying abroad offers you the chance to acquire essential knowledge and experiences that can aid you in your professional life in India and around the world. We trust that this blog has been able to address all of your concerns and provide you with the details you require to decide if studying abroad is the best option for you.

title.rendered: 4 Steps to Defining Your MBA Goals

content.rendered:
Top MBA programs are looking for applicants who have a clear idea of how a business degree will help shape their future. This is why the MBA goals essay is such an important piece of your b-school application.

But how do you write a goals essay if you’re unsure of your post-MBA goals? What if you are changing careers and know you want to obtain the skills provided by a business program, but aren’t sure which career direction you want to pursue your degree? Should you spend time looking into post-MBA options (trying out different jobs or shadowing people in different careers) so that you can submit your application with a secure MBA goal, or is it better to enter a program with undefined goals?

Your post-MBA goals should guide you in the application process – at the very least in deciding where to apply. Not only is it worthwhile spending time finalizing a post-MBA direction, but it’s also required. You need to know why you want to spend a large amount of your time and money before you apply. Not knowing what your post-MBA-goals are could turn your MBA investment into a huge debt with no job to pay it off. Think of your goals as a weathervane – if it’s broken, it spins uselessly in the wind, but when working properly, it points you in the right direction. The following 4 steps will help you define your MBA goals:

  1. Think about what you like and dislike about your current and past jobs. Compile a list of what you’d like more of and what you’d like less of.
  2. Talk to people in jobs that appeal to you. Organize informal interviews or email a list of questions to people you know who have positions that you find attractive.
  3. Think about hiring a career counselor. This short-term investment will pay off when you are able to get into the b-school you want and land your dream job after graduation.
  4. Once you have a better idea of your direction, take a look at the career listings of the bigger employers in those fields. Check out profiles of some of the recent MBAs hired by these companies and see if you can arrange to speak to someone in the positions that appeal to you.

Not having clear goals will leave the adcoms wondering why you’re putting in the time, effort, and money to obtain an MBA. They will also be concerned that you won’t be able to find an internship, or eventually a full-time job because you don’t know what you want to do. But don’t worry – the adcom also recognises that your goals may change over the course of your MBA program. It’s okay to be flexible, but not clueless.

Source: The MBA Tour

If you are planning to study in India, Admizz is the best guide for you. 

For more information, follow us on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter,  Linkedin.

title.rendered: 5 Simple ways to increase your Intelligence

content.rendered:
1. Minimize Television Watching – This is a hard sell. People love vegetating in front of the television, myself included more often than I’d like. The problem is watching television doesn’t use your mental capacity OR allow it to recharge. It’s like having the energy sapped out of a muscle without the health benefits of exercise. When you feel like relaxing, try reading a book instead. If you’re too tired, listen to some music. When you’re with your friends or family, leave the tube off and have a conversation. All of these things use your mind more than television and allow you to relax.

2. Exercise – I used to think that I’d learn more by not exercising and using the time to read a book instead. But I realized that time spent exercising always leads to greater learning because it improves productivity during the time afterward. Using your body clears your head and creates a wave of energy. Afterward, you feel invigorated and can concentrate more easily.

3. Read Challenging Books – Many people like to read popular suspense fiction, but generally, these books aren’t mentally stimulating. If you want to improve your thinking and writing ability you should read books that make you focus. Reading a classic novel can change your view of the world and will make you think in more precise, elegant English. Don’t be afraid to look up a word if you don’t know it, and don’t be afraid of dense passages. Take your time, re-read when necessary, and you’ll soon grow accustomed to the author’s style. Once you get used to reading challenging books, I think you’ll find that you aren’t tempted to go back to page-turners. The challenge of learning new ideas is far more exciting than any tacky suspense-thriller.

4. Early to Bed, Early to Rise – Nothing makes it harder to concentrate than sleep deprivation. You’ll be most rejuvenated if you go to bed early and don’t sleep more than 8 hours. If you stay up late and compensate by sleeping late, you’ll wake up lethargic and have trouble focusing. In my experience, the early morning hours are the most tranquil and productive. Waking up early gives you more productive hours and maximizes your mental acuity all day. If you have the opportunity, take 10-20 minute naps when you are hit with a wave of drowsiness. Anything longer will make you lethargic, but a short nap will refresh you.

5. Take Time to Reflect – Often our lives get so hectic that we become overwhelmed without even realizing it. It becomes difficult to concentrate because nagging thoughts keep interrupting. Spending some time alone in reflection gives you a chance to organize your thoughts and prioritize your responsibilities. Afterward, you’ll have a better understanding of what’s important and what isn’t. The unimportant stuff won’t bother you anymore and your mind will feel less encumbered. I’m not saying you need to sit on the floor cross-legged and chant ‘ommm’. Anything that allows a bit of prolonged solitude will do. One of my personal favorites is taking a solitary walk. Someone famous said, “All the best ideas occur while walking.” I think he was on to something. Experiment to find the activity that works best for you.

Source: Internet

title.rendered: 5 Tips to select the right Engineering branch

content.rendered:
Mechanical, Electrical, Computer Science, or something else? Deciding upon the right engineering stream is quite tricky for both students and their parents.

Most of us go through the same dilemma after clearing different entrance exams. Career options for medical and arts students are relatively clear, however, a lot of thought goes into choosing the right branch in engineering.

Most students go by the job prospects of the field while making this decision, interest and aptitude could get ignored in the process. Besides the most popular branches like Mechanical, Computer, Electrical, and Civil, there are numerous other engineering branches like Chemical, Biotechnology, Aeronautical, Industrial, Instrumentation, Marine, etc. which have a good scope

1. Go for interest, not scope

While we may say that scope of a field keeps changing with time, we see new trends coming up every few years. The reality is, every branch has good scope and opportunities if you perform well in it. Contrary to this, if you take up a branch just based on its job prospects and lack interest in it, you’ll end up getting nowhere.

So it is very important to go for a branch that is of your interest.

2. Branch vs College

It is that time in your life when you have to choose from a platter.

Whether you choose college A over college B or branch X over branch Y should not be a random decision and instead be based on research on these colleges and the electives they offer under each course.

Run through the college websites and the course material they offer under the branch you aspire for to make the right decision.

 3. Specialisation is good

Engineering provides an opportunity to specialize. Choosing one from the various types of engineering disciplines is not an easy job. Digging deeper and knowing more about every branch can help you in making the right choice. It is the same as taking a straight way to your destination or taking roundabouts to get to the same place. The clearer the approach, the better will be the results.

For example, if you are interested in cars, you might as well want to take up Automobile Engineering instead of Mechanical. But the message is: be sure of what you want to pursue.

4. Work life after graduation

It is critical to understand what kind of professional work is expected of you once you take up a job. For instance, Civil Engineering means a lot of fieldwork and if you are not suited for that, you better not choose Civil Engineering in the first place.

Take the example of Mohit, a Biomedical Engineer from Delhi who uses technology to help burn victims recover from their injuries. Mohit loves his job.

He was aware and also realized how the field of Biomedical Engineering is a bridge between medicine and engineering.

5. Options for Post-graduation

If you aspire to do post-graduation and have some ideas already, it might be a good idea to do a quick check on the opportunities for post-graduation.

For example, if you choose to pursue a bachelor’s in Mechanical Engineering, you can do your Master’s in Robotics, Automobile, or Industrial apart from core mechanical opportunities like manufacturing, etc.

But if you do a Bachelor’s in Automobile Engineering, your options for post-graduation become limited.

Source:rediff.com

title.rendered: Are Nepalese youth going abroad coming back to Nepal after abroad studies?

content.rendered:
According to the 2018 Open Doors Report on International Educational Exchange data released by IIE and the U.S. Department of State Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, the number of Nepali students studying in the United States has increased by 14.3 percent over the prior year. 

Nepalese have become the fastest-growing immigrant population in Australia. The population of Nepali students in Australia is the fifth largest among foreigners studying in the country. The number has significantly increased in 2018.

However, there are no statistics to track how many of these youths are coming back to Nepal. It is safe to say that many of the youths that go abroad prefer to stay back rather than come back to the country. There might be many reasons behind it. The familiarity with better facilities, higher income, a better lifestyle, and frustration towards an underdeveloped country might be some of the reasons. 

The story of India is a bit different. Throughout history, students from Nepal have pursued their education in this neighboring country—from the Gurukul system to the inception of modern education in various destinations like Deharadun, Patna, Darjeeling, Banaras, and Gorakhpur. While exact data is not available, as students do not have to acquire a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Education, it is estimated that over 15,000 students leave the country on an annual basis for India. Out of them, most students are found to be returning back to Nepal after their study and internship. Thus, the brain drain threat is quite less among students who go to India for their studies.

title.rendered: Blender Technology – Animation for the Future

content.rendered:
The beauty of technology is that it is always evolving. One software takes over the other and one device takes over another, this is how the world of technology keeps moving ahead. Animation is one field that has garnered quite a lot of attention during the past 25-30 years. From 2D technology arose 3D technology. Ever since the advent of 3D technology, software like MAYA, max labs have been the primary sources of animation. Offered at premium prices, this software required quite a lot of skill and experience to excel at these. 2D animation is still being used mostly for general animation purposes by most firms that can’t bare the heavy costs of Maya technology and skilled personnel. The recently evolving animation technology, Blender is now a new hope that will be useful to take 3D animation to a whole new level.

As defined by Wikipedia.com Blender is a professional free and open-source 3D computer graphics software product used for creating animated films, visual effects, art, 3D printed models, interactive 3D applications, and video games. Blender includes a lot of features like 3D modeling, UV unwrapping, texturing, raster graphics editing, rigging and skinning, fluid and smoke simulation, particle simulation, soft body simulation, sculpting, animating, match moving, camera tracking, rendering, video editing, and compositing. In brief, Blender is a free software for animation that does everything that any other expensive 3D animation can do.

Tech gurus predict that Blender can be the future of 3D animation. They are probably correct. Here is the reason why Blender can take over all the overtly commercial software in the 3D animation industry:

  • It is an open-source project that can be used for personal and commercial purposes for free, without any licensing or copyright issues. There are numerous companies that used pirated versions of Maya now. With the companies taking measures to stop this piracy, obviously, all the Maya users will look for something else, as effective as Maya!
  • Blender manages to do a lot more than much commercial software and can compete even with the big expensive names. Many were scared off by the interface in versions up to 2.49. It looked less polished and was not user-friendly. Starting with release 2.5, Blender has a shiny UI that looks as professional as anyone could wish and the improved functionality and workflow make it friendlier to new and old users.
  • It can render photorealistic quality images by itself or through external renderers
  • It is fast enough and getting faster with each version
  • Because of the not-so-heavy size of the software, it can handle complex scenes without crashing or some disaster happening right before a deadline.
  • It is pretty simple and easy to understand. Unlike the software which seems difficult even after months of training. The only negative points of the blender are that they aren’t usable for architects for visualization. But with better versions coming up frequently we can expect blender to soon become a good tool for architectural visualization. The current complaints regarding layer management, texture mapping, and disabling an object from casting shadows without having to work around too much are also being worked on. There are some tools missing like a proper offset but the developers’ community is working on add-ons that will complement the latest release. So yes, undoubtedly Blender is the future of the Animation industry which is a good place for creative and artistic people. Blender training is now being offered in various institutions and it is a suggested course for upcoming and enthusiastic animators.
  • To search for institutions offering Blender, do download the Admizz app on your mobile or visit Admizz.com. We are a group of young entrepreneurs working on improving the way education is pursued. Admizz is our first step towards better digital education.
  • We, Admizz.com, are the perfect place to search or to get direct admission into all types of colleges, training institutes, and educational institutions. This is our small step towards digitizing the process of admission in the education system. We believe that not only education but also its initial processing should get digitized. Many prestigious institutions are listed on Admizz.com. Not just colleges and schools, information regarding training and coaching institutions is also a part of our website. Students can see the listed institutions in the city of their choice. One can also see the college description, courses oﬀered, fee structure, and also reviews of the selected institution.
  • After getting all these details, students can apply online to get admission to the Institute of their choice. One can save a lot of time, money, and eﬀort by using @Admizz.com. One can also mail us for any support and get assistance from our trained employees. Our vision is to make the admission procedures very simple for students with the use of technology. Admizz.com is managed by INRA EduTech Services Pvt. Ltd. and MKS Technology Pvt. Ltd. in India and Nepal respectively.

title.rendered: Difference between BBA, BMS and BBM

content.rendered:
Basically, Management courses are the subjects that deal with the study of trading and management skills. There are many courses to study under management. Currently, many specializations have also been there under particular courses. 

Let’s compare the three aspects, Skills Taught, Job Prospects, and Average Salary:-

Skills Taught

BBA deals with Management, Leadership, Entrepreneurship, and Marketing Techniques whereas BMS has leadership, Managerial, Marketing, Industrial Skills & Inter-Personal Skills and BBM deals with leadership skills in the business and corporate world. 

Job Prospects

With job placements, BBA graduates can go for Human Resource Executive, Marketing Executive, Marketing Manager, Research & Development (R&D) Executive, etc. As a BMS graduate one can become Banker, Quality Specialist, Business Development, Manager, Teacher & Lecturer, Business Analyst, Finance officer, and Assistant professor as BBM graduates can become HR Manager, Financial Analyst, Operations Manager, Marketing Executive, Executive Assistant, HR Generalist, Business Development Manager, Business Development Executive, etc.

Average Salary

The most comparable is the average package in that case BBA can earn 1-3L INR per annum, BMS can earn 2-7L INR whereas BBM can earn 4-7L INR.

Overall, in BMS, you learn about management, and how to manage the situation in business and trading. BBA awards students with skills in Administration whereas BBM makes the students capable of skills in management aspects. BBM provides specialization in a variety of areas such as Human Resources, operation finance, and marketing whereas BBA does not meet this criterion. 

Here are a few top colleges for management to study in India:

Delhi University, Delhi

VIT Vellore, Vellore

Symbiosis University, Pune

KIIT University, Bhubaneswar

RK University, Rajkot, Gujarat

Jain University, Bangalore

Pune University, Pune

SRM Chennai, Tamil Nadu

MS Ramaiah, Bangalore

Christ University, Bangalore

Amity University, Tamil Nadu

title.rendered: Effective tips for using Technology in Classroom

content.rendered:
Using technology in the classroom often brings an awkward, undesirable mixture. A classroom is filled with distinct individuals and a teacher needs to connect with each one of them. Though we believe in learning to be intrinsically motivated, we expect kids to fare well in tests and examinations.

There is no specialized app for good teaching. Perhaps, there are specific criteria to bring technology into the classroom. Using tech in learning is to obtain educational goals while teachers can also help students use tech as an indicator for learning. The following are a few tips that teachers and even parents need to know about the increasing number of apps in learning.

Prioritize Learning Goals to Technology

The pedagogical goal in teaching and schooling works to convey subject knowledge. It is to help learners make sense of the world. Good teachers are not just subject experts, they are in fact experts in teaching that subject. For any subject, tech becomes an add-on, yet it is not necessarily an integral part of the subject.

Be Open For Discussion about Educational Technology

Using technology in education as a starting point is a way to introduce kids to new experiences and expressions. Choose flexible technology which is relevant and that attracts a student’s inner resources. Let the experiences of a student with technology be open for a talk and should not be constrained. Do not always choose easy apps. Instead, give a chance for kids to get comfortable with messy learning.

Keep Learning Challenging, Do Not Let Tech Make Learning Easy

Use technology in a way to steer students away from things they already know. Challenge them with risks and tasks that can’t be solved with simple steps. Make use of technology which builds the space between what students already know and don’t know. Let learning be a challenging task but not impossible. Find technology that uses questions that promotes curiosity. Bring in genuine student interests Often teachers are seen using social media or popular media for classroom practices. But kids are mostly resistant to such gestures, as they do not approve of having their fun space taken by adults. Rather, it is suggested to connect to kids through interest-driven sites and technology that are genuinely tied to classroom learning. When teachers or adults show interest in the kids’ passion and demonstrate that their skills are relevant to the real world, it brings a profound transformation in kids.

Encourage Conversations

Look for technology that supports social interaction. Consider the technology that promotes conversations. It is not easy to find the right game for all students. It is advisable to get comfortable with the fact that there is no perfect tech solution.

Source: Career India
